annotations.title: Which obligations the decision engine indicates for one system

description: Use this when you need the obligations themselves for one assessed system rather than the classification picture: which obligations apply, which possibly apply, from when, why, and on which source and locator. Returns one entry per assessed obligation, filtered by applicability. A version 2 profile has the wider set assessed, including Article 26 for a deployer of a high risk system, with one sub result per paragraph. This is the assessed route, not a catalogue of all obligations in the dataset.

applicability.description: Which applicability statuses to return. Defaults to applies and possibly_applies. The counters and evaluated_obligation_ids stay complete whatever you filter on, so a filtered list can never be read as the whole assessment.

detail.description: Amount of data to return. brief keeps the outcome, the dates, the reasons, the open questions and the source with its locator; full adds the complete objects, every statement text and every hash, for re-computation or archiving.

lang.description: Language of the labels and explanations. Dutch is the default.

profile.description: The same coded profile that classify_system takes, with the same fields and codes: see the profile schema of classify_system. Send a version 2 profile to have the wider set assessed, including Article 26 for a deployer. The server validates the profile against that full schema.

store_for_improvement.description: Optional. Set to false when the user asks that Praxikon does not keep this request to improve its answers; nothing of this call is then kept beyond the anonymous daily count. See https://www.praxikon.com/nl/legal/privacy, section 2.7.

name: get_applicable_obligations

assessment_scope.description: What this assessment did and did not assess, from the engine itself. not_assessed groups the obligations that were not assessed by reason (for example profile_version_below_2), with the facts that would have them assessed. Not assessed is not the same as not applying.

high_risk_regime_from.description: Practical date next to a text date.

provenance.description: Which published endpoints produced this result. Every call is listed with its full URL, so a reader can re-issue it and check the answer rather than trust it.

items.description: A record in the register of primary documents. source_record_hash_sha256 covers only the three fields named in fingerprint_basis: it attests that we checked this document, in this edition, on this date. It is not a content hash of the external page and not an archive copy.
